output.answer_markdown: Fox Corporation described two types of market risk, changes in interest rates and stock prices [1]. Fixed-rate and variable-rate debt respond differently: a change in rates affects only the fair value of fixed-rate debt, while a change in the rate on variable-rate debt affects interest expense and the cash required to service that debt [2]. Fox had $7.25 billion of outstanding fixed-rate debt, before adjustments for unamortized discount and debt issuance costs, at June 30, 2022 [3]. No variable-rate debt was outstanding as of June 30, 2022 [4]. There were also no borrowings outstanding under the Revolving Credit Agreement as of June 30, 2022 [5].
